page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.16xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-virtualized instance built on Intel x86_64 hardware. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs configured across 32 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz, with 2 threads active per core. System memory totals 256.0 GB, sustaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators.

Networking capabilities are characterized by a 67 Gbps baseline bandwidth, delivering robust data transfer capacity for inter-node communication and network-bound services. The configuration contains no local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring external storage attachments such as network volumes for persistence. Public IPv4 addressing is not included complimentary with the instance.

The architecture balances high network bandwidth and substantial multithreaded compute capacity against the omission of bundled local storage. For deployments where local ephemeral caching is not required, resource utilization remains cost efficient because hardware allocations are focused entirely toward high core density, broad network throughput, and proportional memory. Best-fit use cases include enterprise backend microservices, large-scale CI/CD build farms, batch processing and ETL tasks, and networked database backends.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ib.16xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud instance powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It features 64 vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory. This yields a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core, making it effective for standard compute and memory workloads. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating reliance on remote storage solutions for persistent data. Network throughput is provisioned with a 67 Gbps baseline bandwidth, facilitating high-volume network communication between distributed cloud services. Given its balanced resource footprint and substantial network bandwidth, the m8ib.16xlarge is tailored for large-scale enterprise microservices, high-traffic web applications, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, and relational databases utilizing network-attached storage.
